content.introduction: Tech stocks advanced in Europe and Nasdaq futures edged higher on Tuesday as optimism over AI lab Anthropic's plans for a public debut outshone concerns over elevated oil prices and global bond yields. Oil prices declined on Tuesday as investors focused on signs of recovering crude exports from the Middle East and lingering concerns over potential supply disruptions in the region stemming from the US-Israeli war on Iran. Anthropic warned investors about potentially catastrophic AI risks as it prepares for an IPO that could value it at more than $2 trillion. Meanwhile, US stocks ended the session slightly lower on Tuesday, as government bond yields continued their ascent ahead of inflation and labor market data, while investors assessed comments from Federal Reserve officials for the path of interest rates.

Anthropic warns investors about potentially catastrophic AI risks as it prepares for an IPO that could value it at more than $2 trillion.

 Tech stocks gain on Anthropic IPO optimism, offsetting high oil, yields

Oil prices ​rose on Wednesday after US President Donald Trump denied he would be willing to ease sanctions on ‌Iran as Qatar pushed for peace talks, following a fall in the previous session on a recovery in crude supply from the Middle East.
 US stocks ended the session slightly lower on Tuesday, as government bond yields continued their ascent ahead of ​inflation and labor market data, while investors assessed comments from Federal Reserve officials for the path of interest rates. [...] Tesla has entered into credit agreements totaling $30 billion, including a $20 ​billion delayed draw-term loan facility, according to ‌a regulatory filing on Tuesday.
 China's factory activity returned to ​growth in September, an ‌official survey showed on Wednesday, as easing ​weather disruptions allowed ​factories to resume operations ⁠and a ​global artificial intelligence boom ​supported the industrial sector. [...] Robinhood said on Tuesday it will let users trade some US stocks round-the-clock during ‌weekends, marking its latest effort to keep up as the industry marches toward 24-hour access.
 The dollar stood near this year's high versus the euro on Wednesday and ​was poised for the largest monthly rise against it in 14 months, powered by US growth and rising ‌US interest rates in contrast to the energy and debt worries swirling in Europe.
